observed_problem_fact: Apply all inclusive range additions to a zero array, then return the final maximum.
derived_algorithm: Difference array with two boundary updates per range, followed by one prefix scan.
applicable_contract: Offline range batches and final aggregate computations; an alternative to a dynamic tree only when queries wait until the batch finishes.
time_complexity: O(q+n) for q updates over n positions.
auxiliary_space: O(n) difference lane; integer width must cover accumulated sums.
constraints: This does not provide arbitrary online range maximum queries between updates. Endpoint arithmetic and overflow need explicit bounds. Sparse huge coordinates need event sorting or compression with its own cost.

observed_problem_fact: Insert distinct elements, delete an existing element, and report the current minimum.
derived_algorithm: Array min-heap; arbitrary deletion may scan for its slot or use an explicit value-to-slot index.
applicable_contract: Priority queues and heap kernels; avoid maintaining full sorted order when only the extremum is required.
time_complexity: O(log n) insertion and root deletion; O(1) minimum; arbitrary-value deletion O(n) without a slot index.
auxiliary_space: O(n) heap; additional O(n) index only for faster arbitrary deletion.
constraints: Problem values are distinct and deletion targets exist. Generic priority queues allow duplicates and missing removes. A heap does not provide sorted iteration, predecessor, or range queries.

observed_problem_fact: Return the occurrence count of each query string in a supplied input string collection.
derived_algorithm: Count each distinct key once; hash key/count slots, or sort and compact equal runs before binary-search queries.
applicable_contract: Bags/multisets and grouped count stores; avoid expanding repeated occurrences into retained payload.
time_complexity: Expected O(n+q) with hashing; sort/compact O(n log n) then O(q log d) queries.
auxiliary_space: O(d) retained distinct-key/count store, excluding inputs and outputs; sorting a preserved input needs an O(n) copy and sort workspace depends on algorithm.
constraints: Multiplicity and total-size overflow matter. Counting does not preserve the original interleaving of duplicates; APIs exposing that order need additional information. String hashing/comparison cost depends on key length.

observed_problem_fact: Evict the least recently used key at capacity; get and put must each have average O(1) cost.
derived_algorithm: One shared key/value slot store with lookup index and indexed previous/next recency links.
applicable_contract: Ordered hash owners and bounded LRU caches that require constant expected lookup and recency updates.
time_complexity: Expected O(1) lookup/recency/eviction with suitable hashing; resizing is amortized.
constraints: Both lookup and recency information are needed for this cost bound. Replacing links with an array scan changes update cost to O(C); merely storing links in arrays does not remove the logical ordering structure.

observed_problem_fact: Insert words, test complete words and test prefixes; strings contain only lowercase English letters.
derived_algorithm: Array-indexed or compressed prefix edges; a sorted-array lower-bound test is an alternative for read-heavy compatible lexical ordering.
applicable_contract: Prefix lookup and trie owners; compact edge storage without one general-purpose map per node.
time_complexity: Trie search O(L) with constant-alphabet transitions; sorted-array search O(log n) comparisons, up to O(L log n) character work, and arbitrary insertion O(n) element movement.
auxiliary_space: Depends on live prefix edges or stored keys; dense alphabet lanes reserve unused child slots.
constraints: General strings/key analyzers do not inherit the 26-letter bound. Live prefix maps, ordered navigation, deletion and normalization require extra proof. A prefix tree remains a specialized algorithm when required.

observed_problem_fact: Insert/remove and uniform random selection must each have average O(1) cost.
derived_algorithm: Dense values plus value-to-position lookup; delete by moving the last value into the removed slot and repairing its index.
applicable_contract: Unordered set/slot owners where element positions and encounter order are not observable.
auxiliary_space: O(n) dense payload plus position index.
constraints: Swap deletion changes order and slot identity. It is unsuitable for ordered lists, stable handles, or views exposing physical positions without remapping. The lookup index remains necessary for the stated bound.

observed_problem_fact: Evict minimum-frequency keys, breaking frequency ties by least recent use; get and put must have average O(1) cost.
derived_algorithm: Frequency buckets with recency and slot lookup for the full required bound; a bounded-capacity scan is a separate small-cache tradeoff.
applicable_contract: LFU cache metadata review; remove redundant occupancy while retaining frequency/tie-break information.
time_complexity: Expected O(1) for suitably indexed bucket design; scan-based victim selection is O(C).
auxiliary_space: O(C) for either design, with different indexes and constants.
constraints: The challenge can require MORE indexes than a tiny scanning cache. Frequency overflow/rebasing, factory exceptions, and recency ties remain concrete owner contracts. Do not label a scan implementation an O(1) solution.

observed_problem_fact: Membership add/remove/contains over integer keys from 0 through 1000000, with at most 10000 calls.
derived_algorithm: Direct-address bit words for a genuinely bounded dense domain; otherwise reuse key-only open addressing.
applicable_contract: Bounded-domain membership; enum sets; bitmaps; primitive hash-set alternative.
time_complexity: O(1) bit update/query; initialization or full scan O(U/word_bits).
auxiliary_space: U bits plus word-array header for direct addressing.
constraints: U may greatly exceed live cardinality; this challenge permits a large mostly empty universe. Full 64-bit or arbitrary object keys cannot be used as direct array indexes. No order or multiplicity is represented.

observed_problem_fact: Implement put/get/remove without a built-in hash table; keys and values lie in 0..1000000 and get returns -1 for absence.
derived_algorithm: Value array indexed by bounded key, using a legal absence sentinel; generic variants use open-addressed slots plus safe occupancy encoding.
applicable_contract: Enum/ordinal maps and bounded primitive key maps; common key/value slot kernel.
auxiliary_space: O(U) values and, when needed, presence bits.
constraints: The -1 sentinel is safe only because this problem excludes it as a value. Generic full-domain/null-capable maps need a separate absence representation. Sparse domains may consume more memory than hashing.

observed_problem_fact: set timestamps are strictly increasing; get returns the latest value at or before a requested timestamp.
derived_algorithm: Append timestamp/value pairs and binary-search the upper bound in the relevant history.
applicable_contract: Monotone append histories and predecessor queries, using existing sorted lanes.
time_complexity: Amortized O(1) append and O(log h) predecessor search in a history of h entries.
auxiliary_space: O(h) history; key lookup/directory is separate.
constraints: The increasing-timestamp promise removes arbitrary middle insertion. Out-of-order writes, deletions, general navigation, and expiry are additional contracts. A map of histories still needs a key directory; pooled histories require growth/alias rules.
